question: The WHO Surgical Safety Checklist 'Time Out' step requires which of the following?

answers.text: Surgeon alone confirms the operative site and proceeds

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Time Out requires ALL team members to pause simultaneously — it is a team confirmation, not a solo surgeon check.

answers.text: All team members pause, confirm patient identity, procedure and site, and any critical concerns before the incision

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Time Out is a full-team, verbal confirmation immediately before skin incision: patient identity, procedure, site, antibiotic prophylaxis, imaging availability, and any team member concerns.

answers.text: The anaesthetist confirms fasting status and airway grade before induction

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This describes elements of 'Sign In', performed before induction of anaesthesia — not Time Out.

answers.text: The scrub nurse confirms instrument counts and specimen labels at the end of the procedure

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Instrument counts and specimen labels are verified at 'Sign Out' — the third and final checklist stage, completed before the patient leaves theatre.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the WHO checklist: Sign In (before anaesthesia) → Time Out (all team, before incision) → Sign Out (before leaving theatre). Time Out is the only check that requires the full team to halt and confirm simultaneously.
Well done. Time Out is the critical team pause immediately before incision — all team members must be present and actively confirm. It is the check most likely to catch wrong-site surgery.
